title: One layer lines up inside the frame it sits in
goal: Aligning needs two or more layers today, because a layer on its own has nothing to line up with. When a layer sits inside a frame, it does have something: the frame. Make the Arrange buttons line one layer up against its frame, so a single button centres a label inside a card.
notes: Follow-up from next-align-layers (2026-09-03). Today EditorState.arrangeBoxes needs two boxes and LayerArrangement.canAlign(count:) enforces it. The frame case wants the reference box passed in rather than derived from the selection: LayerArrangement.aligned(_:to:) would take an optional container rect. Frames are next-frames; with that flag off the behaviour is unchanged.
acceptance: With one layer inside a frame selected, the Arrange row is there and its six align buttons are live
Pressing Align Center puts the layer exactly in the middle of the frame, and one undo puts it back
A layer with no frame around it still shows no Arrange row
The row says which thing it is lining up against, so nobody has to guess
